title: routing TTL drift in control plane caused cross-region fallback spike
creator: Asha Patel
description: On 2025-02-18 a routing control-plane TTL mismatch allowed stale region drain markers to persist while proxies believed nodes were healthy. The discrepancy caused a cascade of fallbacks across region and tier policies which then overloaded fallback variants and caused elevated latency and error spikes for some customers for ~90 minutes. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root cause, mitigations applied, and long-term fixes.
timeline: 2025-02-18T09:02Z - Alerts: elevated 5xx rate and median tail latency on route group europe-west-1 observed by SRE dashboard
2025-02-18T09:05Z - Pager triggered for Routing SRE rotation. Initial hypothesis: transient backend overload in europe-west-1

2025-02-18T09:12Z - Investigation: control plane showed nodes draining in west-eu, but dataplane proxies reported nodes as AVAILABLE; observed mismatch in 'drain_tombstone_ttl' vs proxy-side cache TTL
2025-02-18T09:22Z - Mitigation 1: temporarily increased capacity for fallback pool variants in other regions to absorb traffic; adjusted autoscaler to ignore ephemeral metrics

2025-02-18T09:35Z - Root cause signal: reconciliation job that issues region drain markers had a clock skew patch earlier that reduced tombstone TTL in control plane but proxies continue to honor old TTLs cached in-memory
2025-02-18T09:48Z - Mitigation 2: forced immediate invalidation of routing metadata on dataplane via a coordinated push (control-plane -> proxies) and rolled forward a TTL harmonization patch
2025-02-18T10:20Z - Traffic returned to normal for most routes; continued monitoring for 60m to ensure no secondary oscillation
2025-02-18T11:45Z - Post-incident conference call and decision to schedule automated TTL alignment tests and additional monitoring
root_cause: A configuration drift introduced during a migration reduced the control-plane tombstone TTL to 30s while proxies continued to use a cached 300s TTL. This gap created windows where control plane and dataplane disagreed about which nodes were draining, leading to unnecessary routing churn and fallback activations. The migration also removed an idempotency guard in the reconciliation loop which allowed repeated re-issuance of drain markers under congestion, amplifying the cascade.
contributing_factors: Clock skew and rollouts: a rolling patch changed default TTLs without a staged compatibility check
Lack of TTL-alignment test: no automated e2e test ensured control-plane and proxy TTLs remained in sync during migrations
Aggressive fallback policy: tiered fallback rules immediately routed to tier-2/region-remote variants when drain markers appeared rather than allowing short grace periods
Insufficient telemetry: dashboards showed elevated errors but there was no immediate signal showing TTL mismatch in routing metadata
immediate_mitigation: Coordinated push to invalidate routing metadata caches on all active proxies (control-plane trigger) - executed at 09:48Z
Increased temporary capacity on fallback clusters to absorb surge traffic and avoid cascading throttles
Reverted the recent migration that changed tombstone TTL pending compatibility fixes
Enabled a short-term delay (10s) in fallback activation to reduce oscillation while caches reconciled
long_term_fixes: Add a TTL compatibility check to rollout pipeline that gates changes to routing-related defaults
Reintroduce idempotency guard in reconciliation loop to avoid re-issuing drain markers while a previous tombstone is active
Implement an e2e test that simulates control-plane vs dataplane TTL drift and validates graceful behavior
Adjust fallback policy defaults to include a configurable grace window and jitter to reduce synchronized failover
Add a migration playbook for routing metadata changes with step-by-step compatibility validations and monitoring runbooks
monitoring_changes: New metric: routing.metadata_ttl_delta (control_plane_ttl - proxy_cached_ttl) with alert when abs(delta) > 30s
Dashboard panel: routing-cache-coherence showing last_updated timestamps per proxy and control-plane version
Alert: fallback_activation_rate per route group with automated correlation to drain marker churn
Synthetic canary: simulated drain markers injected hourly in staging to validate alignment
postmortem_notes: This incident highlighted a class of failures where control-plane configuration rollouts and dataplane cache semantics diverge. The immediate customer impact was limited to a subset of heavy-traffic customers in EU who experienced elevated latency and transient 5xxs for ~90 minutes. Our mitigations prioritized quick cache invalidation and capacity increases rather than heavy-handed global rollbacks. The long-term work focuses on preventing TTL drifts, hardening reconciliation idempotency, and making fallback policies less brittle to short-lived control-plane transitions.
action_items: Ethan Morales - implement TTL compatibility gate in rollout pipeline - due 2025-03-07
Priya Kapoor - add routing.metadata_ttl_delta metric and dashboard - due 2025-02-28
SRE Team - create a runbook for coordinated cache invalidation and fallback throttling - due 2025-03-05
Platform QA - build e2e TTL drift test and add to pre-release suite - due 2025-03-14
Product - review fallback policy defaults and approve grace-window change - due 2025-03-01
notes: We intentionally kept the emergency rollback limited to the TTL change and avoided a full control-plane rollback to minimize blast radius. Follow-ups include a small cross-functional drill for coordinated cache invalidation to ensure the team is ready for similar events.
